title: Debounce with a fake clock
summary: Collapse a burst of calls into one trailing call, with cancel and flush, tested on a scheduler you control.
prompt: The search box saves a draft on every keystroke; you want one save **300 ms after the user stops typing**.
type Debounced<A extends unknown[]> = ((...args: A) => void) & { cancel(): void; flush(): void };
function debounce<A extends unknown[]>(fn: (...args: A) => void, waitMs: number, scheduler: Scheduler): Debounced<A>
interface Scheduler { setTimeout(fn: () => void, ms: number): number; clearTimeout(id: number): void }
Use **only** `scheduler.setTimeout` / `scheduler.clearTimeout`, never the global timers: the tests pass a
fake clock and move time by hand.
- Every call restarts the wait. `fn` runs once, `waitMs` after the **last** call, with the **last** call's arguments.
- `cancel()` drops a pending call. `flush()` runs a pending call right now (and it does not run again later); with nothing pending it does nothing.
- Leave no timers behind once the call has run.

hints: Keep the pending timer id and the latest arguments in variables the returned function closes over.
On each call: `clearTimeout` the old timer, store the new arguments, start a new timer.
`Object.assign(debounced, { cancel() {...}, flush() {...} })` attaches the methods; flush must clear the timer before running, or the call happens twice.
